questions.question: If a dog is chasing your motorcycle, what should you do?

options.text: Stop until the dog loses interest.
Slow down as you approach, then speed up and leave it behind.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down as you approach, then speed up and leave it behind.
questions.explanation: If a dog is chasing you, slow down and approach it calmly. Then accelerate and ride away. If you encounter a larger animal, brake and be ready to stop.

questions.question: Where should inexperienced riders position themselves when riding in a group?

options.text: At the back of the group.

questions.correctAnswerText: Just behind the leader.
questions.explanation: Inexperienced riders should ride just behind the leader. This allows experienced riders to watch them without making inexperienced riders lead the group.

questions.question: A proper lane position should do all of the following, except:

options.text: Help you set up for turns.
Help you avoid wind blasts from other vehicles.
Place you in another vehicle's blind spot.

questions.correctAnswerText: Place you in another vehicle's blind spot.
questions.explanation: A good lane position should help you see others and be seen. It should help you avoid wind blasts, blind spots, and hazards. Your position should discourage other drivers from sharing your lane and give you an escape route if needed.

questions.question: When a vehicle is passing you from behind, what should you do?

options.text: Stay in the center of your lane.
Stay on the right side of your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay in the center of your lane.
questions.explanation: When being passed from behind or by an oncoming vehicle, ride in the center of your lane. Moving closer to the passing vehicle puts you in danger.

questions.question: How many paths of travel does each traffic lane provide for a motorcyclist?
questions.correctAnswerText: Three
questions.explanation: Each traffic lane gives motorcyclists three paths of travel: the left side, the center, and the right side of the lane.

questions.question: Riders wearing helmets are ________ more likely to survive a crash than riders without helmets.
questions.correctAnswerText: Three times
questions.explanation: At any speed, wearing a helmet makes you three times more likely to survive a head injury in a crash than riding without one.

questions.question: When braking on a slippery surface, what should you do?
questions.correctAnswerText: Use both brakes.
questions.explanation: On a slippery surface, reduce your speed and avoid sudden movements. Use both brakes when you need to slow down or stop.

questions.question: Before your passenger rides, you should instruct them to do all of the following, except:

options.text: Mount the motorcycle after the engine is started.
Sit as far forward as possible.
Keep a large distance between themselves and you.
Keep their legs away from the muffler and chains.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep a large distance between themselves and you.
questions.explanation: Tell your passenger to mount only after the engine starts. They should sit as close forward as comfortable without crowding you. They should hold the handholds or your waist and keep their legs away from the muffler, chains, and moving parts.

questions.question: How should you swerve correctly?

options.text: Press the handle grip toward the direction you want to swerve.
Press the handle grip away from the direction you want to swerve.

questions.correctAnswerText: Press the handle grip toward the direction you want to swerve.
questions.explanation: To swerve around a hazard, apply light pressure to the handle grip in the direction you want to go. To swerve left, press the left grip, then the right to straighten. To swerve right, press the right grip, then the left.

questions.question: When preparing to pass another rider on the left, where should you position yourself?

options.text: In the right part of the lane so they see you in their side mirror.
In the left part of the lane to see better ahead.
In the center of the lane so they see you in their rearview mirror.
Weave in your lane to get their attention.

questions.correctAnswerText: In the left part of the lane to see better ahead.
questions.explanation: When passing on the left, ride in the left part of your lane to see ahead better and be more visible to drivers in the passing lane. Check your mirrors and look over your shoulder before changing lanes.

questions.question: A rectangular sign may be a:
questions.correctAnswerText: Speed limit sign.
questions.explanation: Regulatory signs show rules like speed limits. They are rectangular with white background and black letters or symbols. You must follow the rules on these signs.

questions.question: A linked braking system:

options.text: Connects the front and rear brakes so both brakes work when you use either brake lever.
Connects the front brake to the gear shifter and applies the brake when you downshift.
Connects the rear brake to a foot control.
Connects the rear brake to a switch on the handlebar.

questions.correctAnswerText: Connects the front and rear brakes so both brakes work when you use either brake lever.
questions.explanation: A linked braking system connects the front and rear brakes. When you use either brake lever, both brakes get pressure. Check your owner's manual for details about your motorcycle's braking system.

questions.question: Which of the following is true?

options.text: The front and rear brakes provide equal stopping power.
The front brake is more powerful than the rear brake.
The rear brake is more powerful than the front brake.
Use only the front brake when stopping.

questions.correctAnswerText: The front brake is more powerful than the rear brake.
questions.explanation: The front brake provides about 70 percent of your stopping power. It is more powerful than the rear brake. Always use both brakes when you slow down or stop.

questions.question: About ______ of accidents involve driver inattention?
questions.correctAnswerText: 80 percent
questions.explanation: About 80 percent of traffic accidents happen because drivers are not paying attention.

questions.question: When braking on a slippery surface, you should:

options.text: Use both the front and rear brakes.
Squeeze the front brake hard to stop the front tire from locking.
Use one brake at a time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both the front and rear brakes.
questions.explanation: On slippery surfaces, use both brakes to slow down. Squeeze the front brake gently to avoid locking the front wheel. Use light pressure on the rear brake.

questions.question: Which type of sign is yellow with black lettering or symbols?
questions.correctAnswerText: Warning
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They tell you about road conditions ahead.

questions.question: When packing a load on a motorcycle:

options.text: Put heavier items toward the front.
Put heavier items toward the rear.
Mount loads behind the rear axle.
Store lighter items in front of you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Put heavier items toward the front.
questions.explanation: Place heavier items toward the front of your load. Load everything over or in front of the rear axle. Put lighter items behind you.

questions.question: When riding in a group, inexperienced riders should position themselves:

options.text: At the rear of the group.

questions.correctAnswerText: Just behind the leader.
questions.explanation: Less experienced riders should ride just behind the leader. This puts them near the front of the group so experienced riders behind them can watch them.

questions.question: Which of the following is not a possible cause of a wobble on your motorcycle?
questions.correctAnswerText: Uneven road
questions.explanation: Wobbles usually come from improper loading, unsuitable accessories, or incorrect tire pressure. Do not try to speed up to stop a wobble.

questions.question: If a friend has been drinking alcohol and wants to drive, which of the following should you not do?

options.text: Encourage other friends to talk them out of driving.
Tell them to take less-crowded roads.

questions.correctAnswerText: Tell them to take less-crowded roads.
questions.explanation: To prevent someone from driving drunk, arrange another way for them to get home, involve them in other activities to slow their drinking, find excuses to keep them from leaving before they are sober, and get other friends to help stop them.

questions.question: What should you do on a long trip?

options.text: Take as few rest breaks as possible.
Use caffeine or other stimulants if you feel sleepy.
Wear warm clothing to stay comfortable.
Ride more than 12 hours each day.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wear warm clothing to stay comfortable.
questions.explanation: Dress warmly to protect yourself from wind, cold, and rain. Ride no more than six hours a day. Take rest breaks at least every two hours. Do not use caffeine or other stimulants—they cause extreme tiredness when they wear off.

questions.question: What does this hand signal mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: Slow or stop
questions.explanation: Hand signals show turns or stops. When a rider's left arm is bent at the elbow and points downward, it means the rider is slowing down or stopping.

questions.question: If you cannot avoid hitting an object in the road, what should you do?
questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down before hitting it.
questions.explanation: Slow down as much as possible before impact. Try to hit the object at a 90-degree angle. Keep the motorcycle upright. Rise slightly off the seat. Roll off the throttle a little just before impact.

questions.question: How do you regain control if your rear tire locks up?

options.text: Swerve toward the side with fewer hazards.
Accelerate while the brake is still engaged.

questions.correctAnswerText: Release the rear brake.
questions.explanation: Release the rear brake to regain control of a locked rear wheel. However, if you lock the rear brake on a surface with good traction, you can keep it locked until you stop completely.

questions.question: Which collision does not require a police report?

options.text: A collision where someone is injured
A collision with property damage over $1,000
A collision with an unattended vehicle
A minor accident in a parking lot

questions.correctAnswerText: A minor accident in a parking lot
questions.explanation: Report a collision to police if someone is injured, if you hit an unattended vehicle, or if property damage is over $1,000.
